narrative.overview: A reference shelf for engineers that behaves like a good field guide: a calm, near-monochrome canvas where structure does the talking and colour is used to organise, not decorate. Someone arriving cold from a shared link is oriented in seconds — a dark, textured hero cover states what the tool is, then the page opens into an airy grid of white surfaces to scan and work through. The palette is disciplined slate neutrals with a single saturated accent per tool acting like a coloured index tab; where many things must be distinguished at once, a controlled spectrum is used as labels, never as mood. Interaction turns tactile and confident: surfaces rest on soft ambient depth and lift toward you on hover. The look is deliberately brand-neutral, so external content rides in as content, not as a visual world.
keyCharacteristics: Slate-neutral canvas; one accent per tool used as an organising index colour
Dark, textured hero cover per page over a light, scannable body
White cards with hairline borders, soft ambient depth, and a hover-lift
Inter throughout, with a strong display-to-body scale and tight display tracking
Buildless static pages; consistency carried by shared tokens, not a framework

rules.name: The Index-Tab Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour is an organising signal, never atmosphere. One accent owns a tool; the spectrum only appears where distinct items must be told apart. If a colour isn't labelling or signalling state, it should be slate.

rules.name: The Neutral-Identity Rule
rules.body: No external organisation's brand colours enter the system. Content can name any company; the palette stays slate-plus-accent.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Inter carries display, body, and label. Do not introduce a second family — especially not monospace as a technical costume. Range comes from weight and size.

rules.name: The Tight-Display Rule
rules.body: Display and headline sizes track negative (-0.02em to -0.035em) and stay heavy (700). Small labels track wide (+0.1em) and uppercase. The tracking direction flips with size.

rules.name: The Soft-Lift Rule
rules.body: Interactive surfaces rest on Ambient depth and rise (bigger shadow + translateY(-3px)) on hover, over ~0.2s. The lift is the primary interaction feedback; keep it consistent across cards.

rules.name: The Honest-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow has offset and blur. No zero-blur block shadows, no zero-offset coloured halos standing in for depth.

dos: Do commit each tool to one accent (Indigo or Emerald) and use it as an organising index colour — links, primary action, focus ring, selected state.
Do give every tool a dark Ink-Slate hero cover with the dotted texture and one soft accent glow, then open into a light, scannable body.
Do rest interactive surfaces on Ambient depth and lift them translateY(-3px) with the Lifted shadow on hover.
Do keep type in Inter, with heavy negative-tracked display (-0.02em to -0.035em) and small uppercase tracked labels (+0.1em).
Do pull the first content block up into the hero with a negative top margin for immediate depth.
Do keep the accent scarce — if a colour isn't labelling or signalling state, make it slate.
Do keep new tools self-contained and buildless, inheriting tokens rather than a framework.
donts: Don't adopt any external organisation's brand colours or identity; content names companies, the palette stays neutral.
Don't introduce a second typeface, or use monospace as a technical costume.
Don't use gradient text, hard zero-blur block shadows, or a coloured side-border thicker than 1px as resting decoration (the accordion's open-state bar is the single sanctioned exception).
Don't let the categorical spectrum become mood — it exists to distinguish items, not to fill space.
Don't flatten the depth system: shadows must keep offset and soft blur, never a zero-offset coloured halo.
